obligation: DOE-417 Emergency Alert (cyber event interrupting operations; system shut-down)
citation: Form DOE-417 Schedule 1 criteria 3 and 4; Federal Energy Administration Act of 1974 sec. 13(b) (Pub. L. 93-275); OMB 1901-0288
trigger: Criterion 3: a cyber event (not a NERC Reportable Cyber Security Incident) that causes interruptions of electrical system operations, for example unauthorized SCADA commands that open feeder reclosers. Criterion 4: complete operational failure or shut-down of the distribution system (all 3 feeders out)
deadline: Within 1 hour of the incident. If operations are critical, telephone notice to the DOE Operations Center is acceptable, followed by the written form
notify: DOE (DOE-417 online system; DOE Operations Center by phone as backup)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the cooperative is an electric utility under the form definition. File directly unless the G&T or the Balancing Authority files for it under the written arrangement (P03 G-038). Owner: Line Superintendent

trigger: A Reportable Cyber Security Incident as defined in the NERC Glossary
deadline: Within 1 hour
applies_at_this_tier: No - the term applies to BES Cyber Systems of NERC-registered entities; the cooperative is not registered (P03 G-046). Use criterion 3 instead

trigger: A cyber event that could potentially impact electric power system adequacy or reliability, for example a blocked attempt to sign in to SCADA or to change recloser settings, with no interruption
deadline: Within 6 hours of the incident, if no 1-hour criterion applies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Criterion 12 (loss of service to more than 50,000 customers) cannot be met with about 820 meters

trigger: Significant new information after a filed report; every filed report
deadline: Updates as needed; final report (updated Schedule 1 and all of Schedule 2) within 72 hours of the incident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - owner: Office and Finance Manager, with the Line Superintendent

obligation: Operational notice to the G&T control center
trigger: Any event that changes load at the delivery point or may affect the G&T system, including a mass outage caused by SCADA commands
deadline: Immediately by phone
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and operational, not a cyber reporting rule. Also the first step of the DOE-417 filing arrangement

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Prompt notice under the policy; call the 24x7 hotline before hiring any response firm
notify: Insurer breach hotline (panel counsel and an OT-capable forensic firm)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
trigger: Any intrusion into SCADA or field devices
deadline: As soon as practicable (cooperative target: same day)
notify: CISA (report.cisa.gov or CISA Central); FBI field office
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; brings response help and supports the OFAC mitigation factor

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents, for example name with SSN (CIS, scanned applications) or information about a member's physical condition (medical-needs list in the outage module)
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of a breach (a 15-day extension is possible only for good cause given in writing to the Department within 30 days)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if member personal information was accessed; not expected in an OT-only intrusion. The outage module (medical-needs list) must be checked

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Only if 500 or more Florida residents are affected (the cooperative has about 820 meters)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Only if more than 1,000 individuals are notified (possible only with the scanned applications of former members, about 2,400)

obligation: Vendor breach notice to the cooperative (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent (business suite vendor, AMI vendor, MSP) determines a breach of the cooperative's member personal information
deadline: Within 10 days after the determination; contracts should require faster notice (POL-02 A.5)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in the vendor contracts

trigger: Affected members who reside outside Florida (for example, seasonal residents with an out-of-state mailing address)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residence of affected members

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any payment to an extortionist
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability

trigger: Any incident
deadline: No incident notice requirement found in 7 CFR 1730
notify: RUS General Field Representative (at the General Manager's discretion)
applies_at_this_tier: No legal duty found. Record the incident and lessons for the VRA update and the borrower analysis (1730.22(a), 1730.27(a))

obligation: NERC CIP-008-6 R4 Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
trigger: Reportable incident or attempt involving high or medium impact BES Cyber Systems
deadline: Within 1 hour after determination; attempts by end of next calendar day
applies_at_this_tier: No - the cooperative is not NERC-registered (P03 G-046)

trigger: Attachment 1 events for registered entities
deadline: Later of 24 hours or end of next business day
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a registered entity (P03 G-047)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; coverage under a final rule not assessed

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-designated pipeline
deadline: No later than 72 hours after identification
applies_at_this_tier: No - the cooperative operates no pipelines

trigger: Cyber attack on a power reactor licensee
deadline: 1, 4, or 8 hours depending on the event
applies_at_this_tier: No - no NRC license

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the cooperative holds no federal contracts or subcontracts (an RUS loan is not a procurement contract)

trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts
